channels.title: Channels
channels.desc: One channel per subject, open or private, with a topic and description everyone can read.
channels.long: Each theme gets a channel with a short topic and a description of what belongs there. Open channels can be read by anyone in the workspace; private channels hold the coordination that should not circulate yet.

bullets.b1: Topic and description explaining what belongs in the channel
bullets.b3: Mute a channel without leaving it

threads.title: Threads
threads.desc: Replies stay attached to the message that started them, so the channel stays readable.
threads.long: When a subject needs depth, the discussion moves into a thread and the main channel stays clean. Whoever took part keeps following; whoever did not is spared fifty notifications.

bullets.b1: Reply count right on the root message
bullets.b2: A list of the threads you follow, with what is new

calls.title: Calls
calls.desc: Voice and video from any channel or conversation, with history and duration.
calls.long: The call starts from inside the conversation: same context, same people. When it ends, it lands in the history with duration and participants, so you can reconstruct what was decided.

bullets.b1: Starts from the conversation header, no external link
bullets.b2: History with duration, participants and missed calls
bullets.b3: Microphone and camera controlled on the same screen

search.long: Search covers channels, direct messages and thread replies. The result shows the excerpt with the term highlighted and takes you straight to the message, highlighted in the timeline.

security.title: Security

security.long: Each workspace decides who joins and how long the history is kept. SAML and SCIM on paid plans, with an exportable access log for the security team.

q1.q: Can I import the history from my current tool?
q1.a: Yes. We accept exports from the most common tools and keep the author, date and source channel. Importing a workspace with a year of conversation usually takes an afternoon.

q2.a: No. It covers up to ten people with no end date. The difference to Pro is full history, group calls and external guests.

q3.q: How does billing work when someone leaves the team?
q3.a: Billing is per active person per month. When you deactivate an account, the pro-rated amount comes back as credit on the next invoice.

q4.a: No. Content is used only to deliver the message and feed the workspace's own search. We do not train models on customer conversations and we do not sell data to advertisers.

q5.a: Yes, for Android and iOS, with notifications for mentions and direct messages. The web version is installable and works offline for reading recent history.

about.title: A conversation tool built by people tired of meetings
about.p1: Elo started as an internal project of a ten-person team spread across four time zones. We needed a place where decisions stayed written down and findable six months later — and no tool at the time solved that without turning into a notice board.
about.p2: Today we are 34 people, remote by choice, serving teams that work the same way: more text, less calendar. We still use the product all day, which settles most arguments about priority.
about.privacyIntro: Work conversations carry contracts, salaries and clients. We treat them as such.

encryption.title: Encrypted in transit and at rest
encryption.desc: TLS 1.3 between client and server, and encrypted volumes on disk.

export.desc: Full export in JSON, attachments included, without talking to support.
